page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the server utilizes an Intel processor with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core, providing dedicated CPU allocation. The processor configuration includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average performance across most compute and memory metrics. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1770.0 and a multi-core score of 6838.0. In memory bandwidth testing, it recorded 530.44 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, though uncached large-block reads dropped to 61.33 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark memory scores fell into the bottom 25% tier, indicating potential bottlenecks under memory-intensive parallel workloads. However, database operations and Redis SET performance remain steady, with Redis handling 9.71 million operations per second.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, the n4-standard-8 offers a standard resource density suitable for general-purpose workloads. It is well-suited for web serving, software compilation, and lightweight database operations. While it supports AMX and AVX-512 instructions, its poor performance in medium-sized LLM text generation (6.31 tokens/sec) and lack of GPU acceleration make it less suitable for intensive machine learning inference, though it can handle small-scale model prompt processing.
